svg.text: 日本 · A visual portrait of an island nation
Simplified illustration · positions approximate, not to scale

text.tspan: Japan is an archipelago of roughly 14,000 islands in East
Asia, stretching along the Pacific coast in a graceful arc.
Four main islands — Hokkaido, Honshu, Shikoku and
Kyushu — hold the vast majority of its population and
economic activity, ringed by mountains and coastlines.
Japan blends deep tradition with cutting-edge modernity: neon-lit megacities coexist with wooden shrines and quiet mountain villages, shaped by an
aging population and rapid technological innovation. Its cuisine, design and pop culture have travelled the world, yet many rituals and everyday customs
remain rooted in centuries of local practice — from the tea ceremony and calligraphy to seasonal festivals and the enduring craft of the artisan.
Japan remains among the world's largest
economies, with strengths in automobiles,
electronics, precision machinery and services.
Its nominal GDP in current US dollars reflects
exchange rates as much as growth: after peaking
above US$5 trillion in 2019, a weaker yen and
slower activity pushed the total down to about
US$4 trillion by 2024.

svg.text: Non-Japanese residents ≈ 2.5% of the total; slice sizes exaggerated for clarity.

g.text: Neon-lit megacity — Shibuya, Shinjuku, Akihabara, Asakusa.
Temples, geisha districts, bamboo groves and imperial history.
Japan's kitchen — street food, Dotonbori and Osaka Castle.
Peace Memorial and the floating torii of Itsukushima Shrine.
Iconic volcano, onsen hot springs and lake views.
Northern frontier — powder snow, national parks, fresh seafood.

text.tspan: SOURCES
· GDP: World Bank / IMF (nominal, current US$).
Population composition: Statistics Bureau of Japan & Immigration Services Agency (foreign residents by nationality, approximate percentages).
Map is a stylised illustration, positions approximate and not to scale. Percentages rounded; totals may not sum exactly to 100.
